entries.title: Westfall
body: A fiefdom of the kingdom of Stormwind and once its breadbasket: rolling pastures, wheat fields and farmsteads running down to the long beaches of the Great Sea. For centuries its harvests fed the capital, and its mines and quarries helped build it.

Now the grass is yellow and the fields lie fallow. War, drought and years of neglect wore the land down, and when the Defias Brotherhood made it their refuge, they drove off the farmers, burned and salted the fields, and seized the mines. The Stormwind Guard pulled out when the cost of keeping it became too great. The wind cries over empty farms, carrion birds and rogue harvest golems roam the furrows, and only a few stubborn families remain.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Westfall (introduction, Rise of the Defias, Geography)

entries.title: Sentinel Hill
body: A hill in eastern Westfall crowned by Sentinel Tower, the stronghold of the People's Militia. When Stormwind abandoned the region, the paladin Gryan Stoutmantle raised this volunteer army from the farmers and veterans who stayed, to keep the land free of corruption.

The Militia is made of militiamen, not professional soldiers, and its morale is often low, but it is the only force standing between the Brotherhood and the farmers. Its patrols walk the roads, and its scouts track the Defias across the whole of Westfall.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Westfall (World of Warcraft, Dark Riders)

entries.title: Saldean's Farm
body: The only farm in Westfall the Defias never completely overran. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma have stubbornly refused to leave, though harvest golems walk their fields.
For years their farmhouse has served as a halfway house for travellers and refugees, and the Saldeans do their best to keep their guests alive.

entries.title: Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm
body: A farm in northern Westfall that fell to the Defias and their mechanical harvest golems. The killing machines patrol its fields, and the bandits have moved into its buildings.
Its owners, Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, fled north and now live by the road near the Jansen Stead, close enough to see what became of their home.

entries.title: The Jansen Stead
body: The northernmost farm in Westfall, by the bridge to Elwynn. Like most of Westfall's farms, its owners were driven off by the Defias, and harvest watchers and Brotherhood agents hold it now.
A Private Jansen serves in the People's Militia. Whether he hopes to see his family's land again, no one asks.

entries.title: The Molsen Farm and Jangolode Mine
body: The Molsen Farm, in north-western Westfall, was taken by the Defias like its neighbours, and only harvest watchers tend its fields. A Private Molsen of the Militia may have family ties to it.
Jangolode Mine, just west of it, was one of Westfall's key sources of minerals for Stormwind, until the Brotherhood seized it and set kobolds to dig.

entries.title: Gold Coast Quarry
body: A quarry on Westfall's western coast that was once a valuable mineral and gold mine for the kingdom. As Westfall fell into ruin, the Defias Brotherhood took it over, and its pillagers patrol the workings for their own profit.

entries.title: Alexston Farmstead
body: One of the farms of central Westfall taken by the Defias. Baros Alexston, now the city architect of Stormwind, grew up here and worked these fields as a boy.
Alexston knew Edwin VanCleef well from the years of rebuilding the capital, and remembered him as a peerless fighter, an idealist and a romantic.

entries.title: Moonbrook
body: A small town south-west of Sentinel Hill, once a mining town and the centre of Westfall's farmland. The orcs razed it in the First War; it was one of the last two towns of the kingdom to fall. It was rebuilt after the Second War, only to fall again, this time to the Defias Brotherhood, which drove out its people.

Beneath a barn in Moonbrook lies the entrance to the Deadmines, an old mining network the Brotherhood made its headquarters. Edwin VanCleef chose it because it was secret and secure enough to build his greatest weapon: a juggernaut of a ship meant to destroy Stormwind from the sea.

entries.title: The Dagger Hills
body: A ridge behind Moonbrook, also called southern Westfall. Defias highwaymen, pathstalkers and knuckledusters camp along it, guarding the approaches to their headquarters.
A dwarven brewer, Grimbooze Thunderbrew of the famous Thunderbrew family, keeps a lonely camp in the hills nonetheless.

entries.title: The Dead Acre
body: Once a farm in south-eastern Westfall near the bridge into Duskwood. When the Defias took Westfall they burned the farmhouse and the fields together. Only smoking ruins remain, with harvest watchers stalking the scorched earth.
The ghoul Leprithus rises from its graves at night, a reminder that Duskwood's dead are not far away.

entries.title: The Dust Plains
body: The southernmost reach of Westfall, dry plains where the Riverpaw gnolls keep their camps. On the eastern edge stands Mortwake's Tower, an old mage tower that the Defias have taken over.

The gnolls were once the kingdom's old enemy. In the Gnoll War, seventy-five years before the Dark Portal, they attacked Stormwind itself as a distraction while their raiders burned the farms of Westfall. Now the Defias pay them to do it again.

entries.title: Westfall Lighthouse
body: A lighthouse just off Westfall's southern tip. It was once kept by a human family, until the murloc Old Murk-Eye drove them off. They came back and lit the flame again, and Old Murk-Eye returned with his murlocs; the second time, the family did not escape.
The ghost of Captain Grayson watched them die and could do nothing. With no one else to keep the flame, he has taken the duty on himself, and still stands watch outside.

entries.title: Longshore
body: The long coastline of Westfall, one of the largest beaches in Azeroth. Murlocs swarm along it unchecked, and the wrecks of many ships, elven destroyers among them, lie in the shallows offshore.
Pirates of the Bloodsail Buccaneers have been known to come ashore here too, and fishermen who wander too near the lighthouse have been carried off to be trained as pirates.

entries.title: Gryan Stoutmantle
body: A paladin of the Order of the Silver Hand, born in Westfall. He travelled north to Lordaeron to become a knight, and was there when Prince Arthas purged Stratholme, killing nearly all its people to keep them from the Scourge.

He came home to find Westfall abandoned by the crown and overrun by bandits. Since Stormwind would not defend it, he founded the People's Militia to do it himself. When Lakeshire's magistrate asked him for soldiers, he had to refuse: without the Militia, he wrote, Westfall would fall.

entries.title: Farmer Saldean and Salma
body: The owners of Saldean's Farm, the last farm in Westfall still held by its family. They have watched their neighbours leave one by one, and will not go.
For years their farmhouse has served as a refuge for anyone passing through the fields, and they do their best to keep their guests alive.

entries.title: Theodore and Verna Furlbrow
body: Pumpkin farmers who fled their farm when the Defias and their harvest golems took it. They live beside the road near the Jansen Stead with what they could carry, and are often the first Westfall folk a traveller from Elwynn meets.

entries.title: Captain Grayson
body: The ghost who keeps the Westfall Lighthouse. He was there when the keeper's family died at the hands of Old Murk-Eye's murlocs, and could not save them. Bound to the place, he tends the flame himself and asks the living to make Longshore safe again.

entries.title: Old Murk-Eye
body: An old murloc of Longshore who leads raids along the coast. Twice he drove the keepers out of the Westfall Lighthouse, and the second time none of them survived.

entries.title: Edwin VanCleef
body: The elected guildmaster of the Stonemasons' Guild and one of the architects who rebuilt Stormwind after the Second War; he also led the building of Nethergarde Keep. Mathias Shaw of SI:7 was his childhood friend, and trained him in the ways of a rogue.

When the nobles refused to pay what they owed, and disbanded his guild for demanding it, VanCleef founded the Defias Brotherhood. He swore that the House of Nobles, and the entire kingdom of Stormwind, would pay for their crimes against the Stonemasons. He has become one of the greatest threats the kingdom faces.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Edwin VanCleef (introduction, The reconstruction of Stormwind)

entries.title: The Breadbasket of Stormwind
body: As Stormwind grew, its people spread across the fertile land west of the capital, and Westfall became the kingdom's breadbasket. It suffered for it. In the Gnoll War, gnolls attacked the capital as a distraction while their raiders burned Westfall's farmsteads. Years later a Gurubashi troll war party slipped past the patrols and burned three towns, which led to the Gurubashi War.

In the First War, Warchief Blackhand sent raiders deep into Westfall to spread panic, and whole villages fell. After the Second War the people came home and rebuilt, but the land never fully recovered before the next ruin came.

entries.title: Rise of the Defias
body: When the House of Nobles disbanded the Stonemasons' Guild, the riots that followed killed Queen Tiffin Wrynn. King Varian swore to punish those responsible, and the masons fled into Westfall to escape him. Knowing his anger would never fade, many could never go home.

Behind both sides stood Lady Katrana Prestor, who turned the nobles against the masons' work and the masons against the nobles, and afterwards cut off supplies to Westfall to keep their anger burning. The fugitives became the Defias Brotherhood, wearing red bandanas for the blood of the oppressed, and for a decade they have sown terror across the kingdom, their ranks swelled by the skilled, the desperate and the outcast.

entries.title: Golems in the Fields
body: With Westfall under his control, VanCleef ran the farmers off and took the gold mines. He hired the Riverpaw gnolls as thugs and stationed them across the land, and his men burned the fields and salted the earth so nothing would grow.
When goblins joined the Brotherhood, they brought harvest golems, farm machines reprogrammed to hunt the people of Westfall. They do their job well. Few dare walk the fallow fields alone.
